profile.name: Glenn Maxwell
profile.writeup:
Armed with a breathtaking array of dynamic shots, uncanny spatial awareness, and game-changing athleticism, Glenn Maxwell established himself as one of the most explosive white-ball match-winners in modern cricket history. Emerging from Victoria, the right-handed powerhouse gained the moniker "The Big Show" for his ability to manipulate field placements with audacious reverse-sweeps, switch-hits, and raw hitting power. Maxwell redefined middle-order acceleration for Australia, transforming tight limited-overs contests through his unique ability to clear the boundary from the moment he walked to the crease.


Maxwell eats, sleeps, and breathes the competitive intensity of short-form cricket, bringing an energetic, instinctual mindset to every match. His extraordinary hand-eye coordination extends directly into his secondary disciplines, making him a true three-dimensional cricketer. As a high-calibre off-spinner, his quick arm action and tactical flight allow him to bowl crucial, economically stingy overs in powerplays and middle phases. In the field, Maxwell stands as a generational asset, possessing a lightning-quick slide, an iron-clad pair of hands, and a rocket-like throwing arm that consistently executes direct-hit run-outs from the deep.


His international reputation reached legendary status through extraordinary, history-making World Cup performances. During the 2015 World Cup on home soil, Maxwell struck a 51-ball century against Sri Lanka, then the fastest World Cup hundred by an Australian. He shattered that record at the 2023 World Cup in India by smashing a 40-ball century against the Netherlands, the fastest in World Cup history. Weeks later against Afghanistan, suffering from severe body cramps and unable to walk, Maxwell produced arguably the greatest One-Day International innings ever played, scoring an undefeated 201 off 128 balls to single-handedly chase down 292 from a dire 91 for 7.


Beyond international colours, Maxwell built a formidable reputation across global T20 leagues, becoming a centrepiece franchise player in the Indian Premier League. Representing teams like the Delhi Daredevils, Kings XI Punjab, and Royal Challengers Bangalore, he earned Most Valuable Player honours in the 2014 IPL after scoring 552 runs at an extraordinary strike rate. In Test cricket, despite limited opportunities, Maxwell proved his technical adaptability by scoring a memorable maiden Test century against India in Ranchi in 2017.


His game-changing impact has been recognized with significant honours, including winning the 2015 Men's T20I Player of the Year, the 2016 Men's ODI Player of the Year at the Australian Cricket Awards, and playing an indispensable role in Australia's 2015 ODI World Cup, 2021 T20 World Cup, and 2023 ODI World Cup triumphs. Relentlessly inventive and fearless, Maxwell stands as a modern white-ball pioneer whose boundary-clearing wizardry and big-game clutch performances redefined what is possible in limited-overs cricket.
